caption: Supplementary Table S14. Calibration-threshold workload by block.
notes: Review ratio is (1 − pooled tile-count retention)/(1 − 0.80), assuming every referred tile needs review. The maximum, 2.475, occurred in P1/F3/seed 71: 102 of 202 tiles retained, 100 reviewed. Event-macro coverage was 0.5392, whereas pooled tile-count coverage was 0.5050. Every event-macro value was reproduced from original score files and saved thresholds to numerical tolerance 1e-12. Complete run and event counts are in threshold_denominator_audit.csv and threshold_event_counts.csv. A ratio below one indicates less review than planned and is not evidence that accepted predictions are safe. No analyst time or post-review accuracy was measured.

caption: Supplementary Table S15. Fidelity and retained-set changes under exact binary SDC.
notes: There are 1,320 records per split per block and 33 correlated test event-runs per block. Exact SDC assigns risk one to prediction-empty tiles; all-zero probability fields were not observed. Legacy scores and entropy are reproduced exactly from the frozen checkpoints, and the original v2 weights and scores are reproduced exactly from calibration features. Per-event ordering changes and symmetric differences of retained sets are supplied in ordering_changes.csv. Replacing the stored binary comparator with exact SDC changes pooled-mIoU AURC by at most 0.000028 in P1 and 0.000336 in P2 across individual runs.

caption: Supplementary Table S16. Target-matched comparison with exact binary SDC.
notes: Differences are the named score minus exact SDC. Each row evaluates the corresponding loss functional; both evaluation columns use the same score vector and retained sets. Within an event, the tile endpoint averages tile losses, whereas the pooled endpoint first sums retained confusion matrices. Events are then averaged equally within a run and the nine correlated runs equally within a block. Negative values favor the fitted score under that endpoint. Directional counts are descriptive. All three fitted targets are evaluated under all six endpoints in paired_summary.csv, with every run in paired_effects_by_run.csv; this table displays each target-matched pair. The original v2 row retains its original overlap feature and calibration fit. All three revision refits use exact SDC as the overlap feature.

caption: Supplementary Table S17. Target-matched risk and reference-hazard coverage at nominal 0.80.
notes: All differences are relative to exact SDC and averaged over the same nine correlated runs as Table S16. Hazard coverage is retained reference-foreground pixels divided by full-event reference-foreground pixels. A negative hazard-coverage difference means more reference hazard was deferred to review. This label-informed diagnostic does not select tiles. Nominal coverage uses the original floating-point grid and retains the ceiling count within each event, capped at the event size. It is distinct from applying a calibration threshold. These equal-run summaries differ in weighting from the equal-event-run summary in main Table 4. Full ranges, area coverage and 0.70–0.90 partial integrals accompany the source data.

caption: Supplementary Table S18. Temperature sensitivity of probability-dependent risk components.
notes: Each difference is T = 1 minus calibrated T for event-pooled mIoU AURC; a negative value favors T = 1 for this endpoint. The correlation columns summarize nine correlated test runs per block, and the last column gives the largest absolute run difference. For upper-tail entropy, T = 1 lowers the raw mean score by 0.1125 and 0.0909 in P1/P2, while the nominal 0.80 retained set changes in only one of 33 event-runs per block. This distinguishes probability-score magnitude from selective rank sensitivity. All six endpoints, every run, score differences and retained-set changes are in the accompanying source tables.

caption: Supplementary Table S19. Composite temperature ablation and realized routing coverage.
notes: All differences are the named T = 1 pipeline minus original calibrated v2, averaged equally over nine correlated runs per block. Both AURC columns and nominal 0.80 risk use the mIoU functional. Nominal 0.80 risk is calculated from within-event fixed-count selection, while the last column applies each condition’s calibration threshold to the test split and counts retained tiles across the entire split; it is measured in percentage points. All thresholds retain ties and use the original event-balanced 80th-percentile rule. Updating the calibration mapping and coefficients reduces the average retention displacement in these runs; it does not guarantee attainment of nominal 0.80 coverage under shift. The full-refit pooled-AURC run differences range from −0.00673 to +0.00247 in P1 and −0.00499 to +0.00673 in P2. Complete routing counts, event-macro versus pooled denominators, area and reference-hazard coverage, and partial AURCs accompany the table.

caption: Supplementary Table S20. Class-set AURC displacement for every Kuro Siwo seed and ordering.
notes: Δ is fixed-class minus present-class risk. Relative shift is 100 × ΔAURC / present-class AURC for that row; the overall 32.7% value is the ratio of the mean displacement to mean present-class AURC, not the mean of the six percentages. All rows reuse the same test tiles/events. The six rows are paired descriptive results, not six independent geographic replications or a confidence interval.

caption: Supplementary Table S21. Fixed review count versus calibration-threshold routing on unchanged v2 scores.
notes: Δ is fixed count minus threshold on the same run. Risk is 1−mIoU; a negative risk change means lower retained-set error. Batch risk uses the full-batch fixed class set. Hazard is reference water in P1/P2 and flood in E1; pp denotes percentage points. E2/E3 have no frozen per-tile confusion counts in the audit package, so pooled risk and content are not estimated for those blocks. Means and ranges summarize correlated runs, not independent replications or confidence intervals. All 27 paired values are supplied in paired_by_run.csv.
